thread.title: Netflix: As Analysts Get Back on Board, Fresh Reasons Pop Up - Barron's

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Netflix: As Analysts Get Back on Board, Fresh Reasons Pop Up - Barron's
text:
Illustration: courtesy of Netflix By David Marino-Nachison Aug. 24, 2018 10:40 a.m. ET Shortly after one analyst pointed to Netflix ’s (NFLX) tests meant to find a way around Apple ’s (AAPL) app store fees as a reason for near-term optimism , another echoed that theory—while naming few others that have them saying it’s time to get off the sidelines.
And one of those isn’t one that comes up much, since investors are mainly focused on subscriber numbers. (Or, if they’re more cautious, free cash flow and burn.)
Newsletter Sign-up But SunTrust Robinson Humphrey on Thursday added the notion that high-margin licensing could yield more than a billion dollars in operating profit within a decade. This isn’t a new concept, but it’s also not one that seems to have been central to many investors’ thinking lately.
“Netflix should a have long-term opportunity to grow consumer merchandise licensing revenue and profit while also using it as a way to drive (and fund) content and platform awareness and buzz,” they wrote. (At $1 billion around 2026, that would be some 18 times their estimate of last year’s figure.)
They upgraded the Barron’s Next 50 stock to “buy” from “hold,” setting a $410 price target on the shares—17% above current levels and about 11% higher than FactSet’s mean—while noting their dip since the company reported Q2 results in July . (Their previous target was $415.)
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 Other analysts have lately been getting back on board, too. SunTrust’s report comes as Imperial Capital suggested that the aforementioned sign-up tests might an indication of strong current subscriber growth, boosting their EPS estimates. And earlier this week, MKM Partners called the stock a “ must-own for growth managers .”
Some of SunTrust’s arguments in support of Netflix, meanwhile, were more conventional—which, probably makes sense, as investors may not be thinking about
They also cited optimism about subscriber tests that may be implied by the billing tests Imperial mentioned, said their tracker of domestic subscriber growth has them thinking Q3 could come in ahead of guidance, and cited India as a crucial market if the company can find ways to counter built-in challenges regarding broadband adoption and a market accustomed to paying less for TV services.
